summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (JTM 5.2/53)

data.turoyo: komər, aṯi ḥəlle kəle sanduqo mbasməro <...>
data.translation: Er kam und sah, da ist eine zugenagelte Kiste. <...>

rationale: First Detransitive Part. Pass. box; chest as patient in a short presentative context.

summary: New box Part. Pass.: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC NE Story of Dawid/13)

data.turoyo: <...> Komōd lu… lu+sayfayḏe, koḥoyar kalé mbasmro.
data.translation: <...> He reaches for … for his sword, he sees, hey, it’s nailed in.

rationale: Second new Detransitive Part. Pass. example; source overtly identifies the sword and its persisting nailed state.
Two independent result-state descriptions supply the previously absent Detransitive Part. Pass. section.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (MAC NE Story of Dawid/11)

data.turoyo: <...> Hedik̇a azzé gab qənaġčiye, mbasmaḷḷe i+k̇alane ŭ i+šəlfk̇e bәḥḏoḏe.
data.translation: <...> Then he went to a quartermaster’s office, he nailed the sheath and the blade together.

rationale: Sparse Preterit cell; coordinated objects and reciprocal attachment, with printed lateralization retained.

data.turoyo: Səmle qayiqe bu sayfo w basmirole b qayse, basmore d qayse, šuʕole mlaf lalġul w naḥət bi qayəq.
data.translation: Da zimmerte er mit seinem Säbel eine Barke und nagelte dieselbe mit Holznägeln zusammen; dann verpichte er sie von innen und setzte sich hinein.

rationale: Unusual unprefixed basmirole beside m-initial forms; explicit boat object and wooden pegs.

data.turoyo: <...> Xəṣuṣi d azze li ifada, d šqəlle i ifadayḏe d mgargašše, d ṣləwwe, d mbaṣmarre, dani kulle kito.
data.translation: <...> Specifically, that he went to the interrogation, that they took his statement, that they dragged him about, that they crucified him, that they nailed him up; all of those are there.

rationale: The Preterit cell remains thin after the original example and two round-1 additions. Adds 3pl mbaṣmarre in a religious narrative, preserving source ṣ and the inherited stem I.

summary: Check and correct transposed consonants in the hammer name
rationale: The supplied 94/14 has 'b ač čaʕvkat', with ʕ before v; the entry reverses them. This is beyond clitic or accent normalization. The parallel quotation under črx repeats the entry's čavʕkat, so the proposed correction rests on the supplied corpus reading rather than independent agreement of both witnesses.

summary: The quadriliteral remains stem I as in the existing entry; the new material does not re-label it Q. Preterit basmirole lacks initial m-, while mbasmaḷḷe illustrates lateralization of root-final r before the agent suffix.
Active nailing of blade and sheath at MAC NE Story of Dawid/11 precedes the sword result state at /13. The latter is Part. Pass. with presentative kalé, without an expressed agent.
Material/tool b- and attachment b- occur with different dependents; reciprocal bәḥḏoḏe links the nailed objects. They do not require separate senses.
At 2/83 the input verse has mbasmarli and the inherited quotation mbasmalli. This may be editorial or dialectal; preserve both and ask before a fix-text correction.
The two exact existing citations 2/83 and 94/14 are not repeated. No new idiom is proposed.

The written form mbaṣmarre retains initial m- and has -rre with plural agents. Its emphatic ṣ differs from inherited bsmr/mbasmər; preserve this attested spelling without normalising the root or the base forms. The coordination with ṣləwwe supports an active Preterit, not the round-1 Detransitive result-state section.
Confirm Detransitive Part. Pass. rather than Detransitive Preterit for mbasmro at MAC NE Story of Dawid/13; -o and kalé support the present filing.
Is mbasmalli in the inherited 2/83 quotation an intentional assimilated variant, or should it be corrected to source mbasmarli?
Does unprefixed basmirole at PrS 18/23 represent a dialectal quadriliteral base or a transcriptional omission?
Is ṣ in mbaṣmarre at Jan 2.31/5215 an intentional pronunciation/spelling variant of bsmr or a transcription issue? One token does not justify changing the inherited headword.

Nailing a human participant in the sequence ṣləwwe, mbaṣmarre extends the participants of ordinary nageln; the adjacent crucifixion verb does not establish a separate meaning for bsmr. The identity of the affected person is contextual, not overt in this verse.
